title: Runtime executor advertisement: the executor a runtime role is served by, so a reply is dispatched only to a runtime that can execute its grant
why: A grant pinned to service mode names one exact executor tuple (A35, migration 0067). A runtime advertising the conversation role on that route said nothing of its executor, so the newest ready runtime was chosen even when only an older one ran the pinned executor; the chosen one refused the command (reply_executor_mismatch) and the reply failed although a compatible runtime was available (#393 discussion 4302482626).

A role may now state the executor that serves it, with exactly A35's RuntimeReceipt.executor shapes: service {execution, routeId, executorArtifactDigest}, or native {execution}. A service executor's routeId is the role's route. id, route and presetDigest keep their meanings: presetDigest stays the role's instruction identity and is never an executor digest.

It is a claim the server keeps with the runtime's hello and uses before binding a reply and again before dispatching its create: a pinned service grant is dispatched only to a runtime advertising its exact tuple. A role without the field is legacy or unknown: it keeps native behaviour and is never eligible for a pinned service grant.

value.description: The executor serving this role, as the runtime claims it (A35's shapes). Absent: legacy or unknown, never eligible for a pinned service grant.
